scope: Bounded comparison of pinned source definitions with existing mathematical theorems and two short corollaries. Source-file hash verification is not a Lean kernel build or global proof verification.
status: local word, coordinate, gauge and measure dictionary checked; ordinary mathematical compatibility and original-parameter positivity proved
inputs: full contracted-matrix intertwining on a common invariant coefficient class
polynomial operator preservation of the coefficient class
explicit fresh-index signed recurrence and nonzero scalar denominators
output: For every defined finite residue word on the smooth invariant coefficient class, sum_a beta((R_w F)_a,H_a)=C_r^(-1)<R_w^rad Phi_F,Phi_H>. The original common-cut and parameter-separation hypotheses give local compact and smooth finite-decay positivity.
pending: No claim of identification with every global source form.
Extension from smooth coefficients with finitely many required seminorm bounds to all source classes having only finite differentiability has not been established here.
Global orbital-energy, arithmetic nonvanishing and divisibility, and bounds uniform in growing ranks remain outside this local result.
uniformity: For fixed place, rank, representations and Haar measures, one positive pairing constant works for all words and auxiliary dimensions. Finite decay indices may be chosen for a fixed rank and length bound; operator-norm constants need not be uniform over parameters. No growing-rank or global-energy bound.

dictionary.source_list_order: Tail first: chronological step j in {1,...,h} is original source list index h-j. Rename auxiliary factors by this permutation; do not commute operator factors.
dictionary.partial_transpose: Transpose only the main two-by-two index before insertion at the fresh auxiliary factor. No general reversal of noncommuting old coefficients is used.
dictionary.projection: First component of End(V) x End(V)^op; preserves sums, products and complex scalar multiplication. The recorded second component gives the formal adjoint.
dictionary.coordinate_operators: p=c*d/dc, pb=conj(c)*d/dconj(c), plus coordinate and inverse-coordinate multipliers. Paired p has second component -pb.
dictionary.open_cell: e_a maps to c_a*f_a, f_a maps to conj(c_a)^(-1)*e_a, and middle space maps by m, exactly manuscript b(c,m).
dictionary.pairing: Finite component sum of the Hilbert-Schmidt pairing, linear in its first argument, integrated against a fixed compatible terminal Haar measure.
dictionary.source_normalization_constant: Cst=C_r^(-1)>0, chosen before the word and auxiliary dimension.
dictionary.source_domain: Nonzero outer coordinates, embedded terminal group, positive terminal Gram; functions vanish outside and are smooth locally on that domain.
dictionary.source_parameter_hypotheses: Real original parameters, one common cut with margin two and 1 <= l <= k, and all original pairwise distances >2. Interlacing identifies p_rho, q and sign (-1)^(k-l). The cut-index range is explicit in the source actual-positivity endpoint.
dictionary.zero_denominators: Human residue formulas use nonzero scalar denominators. The polynomial naturality identity permits arbitrary scalar coefficients, including explicit use of the source total-division convention; positivity excludes these singular words.

proof_reductions.claim: one compatibility identity for every finite ordered polynomial
proof_reductions.proof: Intertwining passes from each entry to sums and ordered products; coefficient-class preservation permits applying the scalar pairing identity to PF,H; finite component summation leaves the constant unchanged.
proof_reductions.label: ji-word-pairing

proof_reductions.claim: source original-parameter positivity without stronger shifted separation
proof_reductions.proof: rp-parameter-signs gives the signs and initial nonvanishing at lambda-1,lambda,lambda+1; original distance >2 implies re-word-domain; rp-recursive-positive and re-density give terminal positivity; ji-fused-congruence and ji-rank-descent yield compact positivity, and ji-finite-decay-positivity extends it.
proof_reductions.label: ji-unshifted-positivity

nonimplication.interpretation: Original separation greater than two does not imply shifted separation greater than two. The earlier shifted-hypothesis theorem is retained; a separate corollary covers the source hypothesis.

scope: hypotheses of congruence and rank descent
